# Review of the RTO-6 state model ## What is wrong **Safety-critical gaps** 1. **Low temperature in PROCESS only raises burner fire.** If TT-601 drops below 760 C while fumes are still being admitted, solvent goes through an under-temperature chamber, which is an emissions exceedance. The burner may also be unable to recover (flame loss, fuel problem). High fire should be a first stage only, and the model needs a second stage that isolates the fumes. 2. **XV-602 (bypass damper) is never mentioned.** No state defines its position. The model needs it open and XV-601 closed in OFF, PURGE, HEAT-UP, READY, COOL-DOWN and FAULT. It also needs a defined transfer sequence when entering and leaving PROCESS. 3. **READY to PROCESS is a bare HMI command.** Opening XV-601 needs hard permissives, enforced in logic and not just in the faceplate: - flame proven - combustion fan running and airflow proven - TT-601 above setpoint, with a minimum soak time - inlet LEL below the limit - CL-6 ready to send fumes - no active trips - XV-602 and XV-601 positions proven by limit switches 4. **There is no burner sequence.** HEAT-UP does not include: - pilot and main ignition - trial-for-ignition timing - flame supervision - fuel pressure and valve proving Flame failure has no defined response, and a relight must go back through purge. 5. **Purge is only a timer.** The 5 min should run only while purge airflow is proven, with dampers and valves in position. The timer should reset if airflow is lost. Confirm that 5 min meets the required number of volume changes for the system (NFPA 86 or your site standard). 6. **There is no over-temperature or high-LEL handling.** Solvent loading raises chamber temperature, and there is no high-temperature response and no LEL response (alarm, then divert to XV-602, then trip). 7. **"Any state to FAULT" is too coarse, and FAULT has no exit.** - Different trips need different safe states. Flame failure needs gas off and a re-purge. Over-temperature needs the fan running to cool. Fan failure needs fumes isolated. - A single FAULT state must not stop the fan when the chamber is hot. - The model has no reset path (cause cleared, operator acknowledge, then post-trip purge). - The trip logic should live in the hardwired BMS or safety system, not only in the PLC state machine. **Sequencing and robustness gaps** 8. **Stop in PROCESS goes straight to COOL-DOWN.** It should first close XV-601, open XV-602 and tell CL-6 to stop sending solvent. The model also has no "stop fumes but stay hot" path back to READY. 9. **There are no Stop or abort transitions from PURGE, HEAT-UP or READY.** 10. **There are no timeouts.** HEAT-UP, PURGE and COOL-DOWN each need a time limit, with an alarm or fault if exceeded. 11. **760 C is used as both the entry and exit threshold.** This chatters. Use a deadband with a delay. 12. **Temperature loss in READY is not handled.** It should go back to HEAT-UP, and fumes must not be admitted. 13. **TT-601 is a single point of failure.** The model has no bad-signal check. Use redundant or voted thermocouples for permissives and trips. 14. **OFF to PURGE has no start permissives.** Examples are no active trip, fuel pressure OK, fan available, and valve positions proven. 15. **COOL-DOWN has no fan requirement.** The fan must keep running until TT-601 is below 200 C, and then it can stop in OFF. 16. **Regenerative cycling is not covered.** I assumed bed-switching valves are handled elsewhere. If not, they need to be part of the model. ## Corrected state model Setpoints marked * are placeholders. Set them from the permit, vendor data and the NFPA 86 review. **Safe-state outputs (all states except PROCESS):** XV-601 closed, XV-602 open, and burner gas valves closed unless the state calls for fire. | # | From | To | Condition / actions | |---|------|----|---------------------| | 1 | OFF | PURGE | Start, with permissives: no trip, fuel pressure OK, fan available, XV-601 proven closed and XV-602 proven open. Starts the fan. | | 2 | PURGE | HEAT-UP | Purge timer (at least 5 min, or the calculated volume changes if longer) is complete. The timer runs only with airflow proven, and resets if airflow is lost. | | 3 | HEAT-UP | READY | Flame proven (after pilot, trial-for-ignition, and main flame sequence), TT-601 ≥ 760 C + deadband* (valid signal), held for the soak time*. | | 4 | READY | PROCESS | Operator command and all permissives true: flame proven, airflow proven, TT-601 ≥ setpoint, LEL OK, CL-6 ready, no trips. Sequence: open XV-601, prove it open, then close XV-602 (or the order that avoids a pressure upset). Failure to prove either valve within its time limit goes to FAULT. | | 5 | READY | HEAT-UP | TT-601 < 760 C − deadband*. Fumes remain isolated. | | 6 | PROCESS | PROCESS (stage 1) | TT-601 < low-alarm* (above 760 C): high fire and alarm. | | 7 | PROCESS | READY or HEAT-UP | TT-601 < 760 C for more than t*: close XV-601, open XV-602, signal CL-6 to stop solvent, log the emissions deviation. Go to READY if recovered, otherwise HEAT-UP. If flame is lost, go to FAULT. | | 8 | PROCESS | READY | Operator "Stop fumes": isolate fumes as in row 7, burner stays on. | | 9 | PROCESS | PROCESS (divert) | LEL high alarm*: alarm and reduce load. LEL high-high* or TT-601 high*: isolate fumes (XV-601 closed, XV-602 open), burner off if over-temperature, go to FAULT. | | 10 | READY, HEAT-UP, PURGE | COOL-DOWN | Operator Stop (PURGE can go to OFF if the chamber is cold). | | 11 | PROCESS | COOL-DOWN | Operator Shutdown: isolate fumes first (as in row 8), then burner off, fan stays on. | | 12 | COOL-DOWN | OFF | TT-601 < 200 C: stop fan. If TT-601 is not below 200 C within the time limit*, raise an alarm. | | 13 | Any state | FAULT | Any trip. On entry, apply the trip-specific safe state:
• **Flame failure:** gas off, fumes isolated, fan on.
• **Over-temperature:** gas off, XV-602 open, fan on.
• **Fan or airflow loss:** gas off, fumes isolated.
• **TT-601 bad signal:** treat as a trip. | | 14 | FAULT | PURGE | Cause cleared, operator acknowledge and reset. If the chamber is still hot, run cooling first. | | 15 | HEAT-UP, PURGE | FAULT | Timeout exceeded, with the timeouts set per state*. | **Other notes** - The safety trips (flame, over-temperature, LEL, airflow) should be hardwired in the BMS or safety PLC and be independent of this state logic. - Fail positions should be XV-601 closed and XV-602 open on loss of power or air. - The 760 C minimum comes from your permit. Confirm the low-alarm, soak, deadband and LEL values with the vendor and the permit. If you share the P&ID, the permit's minimum-temperature wording and the vendor's sequence document, I can tighten the setpoints and the trip table.
